usersInfo.title: Users Info Pattern
usersInfo.overviewText1: This page demonstrates a realistic users list: server-prefetched React Query data, nuqs-driven URL state (search, sort, page, page size), a shadcn/ui data table, and a consistent server + client hydration pattern.
usersInfo.overviewText2: Server prefetch runs inside the loader and hydrates the QueryClient cache. On the client, useSuspenseQuery reads from the cache without refetching on first render. If the user navigates away and comes back, staleTime keeps the cache fresh.
usersInfo.overviewText3: nuqs parsers drive query-params: `q` for search, `sort` / `dir` for ordering, `page` / `pageSize` for pagination. Query state and server state live separately — editing the URL always updates the data because the hook is used as the single source of truth.
usersInfo.overviewText4: TanStack Table is configured server-side: `manualSorting`, `manualPagination`, and a row count from the server. Columns reuse the `formatLabel()` helper so enum values stay consistent across the app.
usersInfo.overviewText5: Everything here is reusable: copy the `users/_components` folder, swap the API calls, and you get a new paginated, sortable, searchable table in minutes.
usersInfo.serverPrefetchText: Inside the page loader we call `queryClient.prefetchInfiniteQuery` (or `prefetchQuery`) with the same query key used on the client. The hydrated cache is serialized as `<Hydrate>` and rehydrated on the client with `<HydrateOnClient>`.
usersInfo.urlStateText: All table controls live in the URL: `?q=&sort=name&dir=asc&page=1&pageSize=10`. Typing in the search box updates the URL; updating the URL updates the query. Bookmarks and back/forward work out of the box.
usersInfo.patternComparison: Products use server-side rendering to fetch and pass data to the table. Users use server prefetching and client hydration, which also enables background refetching, shared cache, and optimistic updates.
usersInfo.patternText1: 1. Define a query key factory (e.g. `usersKeys`) so server and client share the same key shape.
usersInfo.patternText2: 2. In your loader, prefetch with `queryClient.prefetchQuery(usersKeys.list({ ... }))` and dehydrate.
usersInfo.patternText3: 3. On the client, call `useSuspenseQuery(usersKeys.list({ ... }))` with the same inputs — the cached data is used immediately.

reactQueryInfo.title: React Query Pattern
reactQueryInfo.serverPrefetchText: Data is prefetched on the server using getQueryClient().prefetchQuery(). The dehydrated state is passed to HydrationBoundary so the client starts with cached data and avoids a loading spinner on the first load.
reactQueryInfo.queryOptionsText: Query keys and fetch functions are defined in a shared queryOptions() object. Reusing it for server prefetch and client hooks keeps them in sync.
reactQueryInfo.suspenseText: The client uses useSuspenseQuery(), which integrates with React Suspense. With server prefetching, data is ready immediately; Suspense shows a fallback on later navigation when the cache is stale.
reactQueryInfo.optimisticText: Mutations can optimistically update the cache before the request completes. If a request fails, the previous state is restored; after it settles, the query is invalidated to fetch fresh data.
